page.text:
A conjecture belongs in a mathematical library only when its statement is
precise and its unproved status is unmistakable. The examples below are
not included as curiosities. Each arises naturally from structures
developed earlier, and each illustrates the gap that can remain between
overwhelming evidence and proof. Verification of finitely many cases,
however extensive, cannot establish a universal assertion about all
integers or all complex zeros.
